This keeps the 1966 terminals, cuts and corners.\n- **Even-stroke layer:** a constant-width stroke drawn along each letter's centre line. Where curves or diagonals would otherwise come out thin, it fills them out, but it can only add up to 4 units per side, so it can't round off ends.\n\nAfterwards I square the same corners as in Series E: the stem ends of a, b, d, u, g, m, n, p, q and r, the f and t crossbars, and the top of the x. Lowercase stems now match each series' capitals:\n\n| Series | Width vs E lowercase | Capital stem | Lowercase stem |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| B | 0.65 | 91 | 91\u201392 |\n| C | 0.78 | 102 | 101\u2013103 |\n| D | 0.89 | 110 | 108\u2013111 |\n| E | 1.00 | 122 | 123 |\n| F | 1.10 | 132 | 129\u2013133 |\n\n**Limitations**\n- **Sharpness.** At large sizes the derived widths aren't as crisp as E. Curves like o and c are slightly uneven, and the tops of v, w, x and y and the t's crossbar are a little soft. That's because narrowing is still done on a picture of each letter, not on the outlines. Now each counter ellipse is adjusted so the stroke across it is the series weight, as a uniform pen would draw it:\n- **a:** the arc's top, between the upper ellipse and the two counter ellipses below it.\n- **f:** the hook's top, between the large ellipse and the small one.\n- **t:** the tail's bottom, between the blue ellipse and the orange circle.\n\nThe counter's other edge, where it meets the stem or the drawn shape, stays where it was. At E(M) weight these letters are unchanged, because there the series weight is the full 1966 weight.\n\n**e and h**\n- **e:** above the crossbar, the right side can no longer bulge past the end of the crossbar. It now rises from the bar's end.\n- **h, n and m:** each arch is clipped to the outside edge of its right leg, so the curve can't swell past the leg where they join.\n- **u:** the same rule at its left leg.\n\nSpacing is recalculated so each lowercase alphabet still matches its 2000 total width.",

It's an export of the values the build currently calculates, so editing it won't change the fonts. Making it the build's actual input would mean reorganising the generator to read these values instead of measuring the scans each time. That's quite doable, and once it's done your edits would go straight into all six widths. I'd suggest it as the next step if you want to edit by hand.\n\n**Conventions**\n- **Units:** font units, 1,000 per em.\n- **x:** measured from the left edge of the 1966 letter.\n- **y:** measured up from the baseline.\n- **Ellipses:** given as centre (`cx`, `cy`) and half-width and half-height (`rx`, `ry`).\n- **Terminal and stem cuts:** a point on the cut and its angle in degrees.\n- **Pen profiles:** 24 pairs of angle around the inner ellipse (0\u00b0 is the right, 90\u00b0 the top) and stroke thickness from there out to the outer edge.\n\n**Series table.** For each width it gives:\n- the width factor `f`;\n- the stroke weight `T`;\n- the per-side spacing adjustments for lowercase, capitals and figures.\n\n**How a width is made from the data:**\n1. Multiply every centre-line x position by `f`.\n2. Draw the strokes at weight `T`; heights stay as drawn.\n3. Scale pen profiles by `T`/140, or so that the stroke where a curve meets a stem comes out exactly `T`.\n\n**What's recorded for each letter**\n- **Bowls (a, b, d, p, q):** outer and inner ellipse, pen profile, stem edges, and the slanted cut with the square stem end.\n- **c and e:** their own ellipse pairs and pen profiles, plus terminal cuts. The e has separate top and bottom pairs and its crossbar heights.\n- **g:** the bowl (same as q), stem, tail ellipses including the 0.81 inner scale, tail pen profile, and terminal.\n- **n, h, u:** stems and the arch ellipse pair with its profile. m and r are marked as reusing the n's arch.\n- **a, t, f:** the ellipses from your screenshots, converted to font units, plus stems, crossbars and cuts.\n- **k, v, w, x, y:** the centre line of every straight stroke and its height range. The w also has its join-trim settings.\n- **i, l, j, z:** described with their key measurements.\n- **s:** listed as traced, since it isn't constructed.\n\n**Where the file and the build don't quite line up**\n- **Arches of n, h, m and u:** the build re-centres the inner ellipse to span the space between the stems in each width. The file records the 1966 measurement, which is why the ellipses in the PNG sit slightly off the counter for n and h.\n- **j:** its tail is a placed segment of the p's bowl ring, so the file describes it rather than giving its own ellipses.\n- **z:** the file gives its rules rather than coordinates, since the build calculates the bars and diagonal for each width.",
